minutes.headline: Appraisal finds the 925 Mass Ave property has a negative value, complicating the town's redevelopment plans
minutes.summary: A light agenda after town meeting: the board approved a student civics-class art event (pending integration into the Spring Fair), an APR land lease for shed display at Lanni Orchards, an appointment to the 300th Anniversary Committee, and ratified a new Outreach Coordinator. The Town Manager reported that an appraisal valued the 925 Mass Ave site negatively given remediation costs, and the board tabled decisions on the Leominster Road right of first refusal and on selling or holding the Hollis Road properties for another week.

what_happened.line: An appraisal found the 925 Mass Ave site has a negative highest-and-best-use value once remediation costs are weighed against market value, the Town Manager reported.
The board tabled a decision on the right of first refusal for 35 Leominster Road until all board and committee recommendations, including Open Space, are in.
The board also tabled whether to sell or hold the 250 and 356 Hollis Road properties for one more week to review the planning board's discussion.
The board voted unanimously to appoint Mora Lizak to the 300th Anniversary Committee and to ratify Jonathan Francis as Outreach Coordinator.
The board also approved a student civics-class art event near the library field and a small APR land lease at Lanni Orchards for shed display.

why_it_matters: The 925 Mass Ave appraisal means the town cannot count on selling the site to cover cleanup costs, so any redevelopment there likely depends on outside grants or credits.
The delayed calls on Leominster Road and the Hollis Road properties are land-use decisions that could shape future town holdings and will come back to the board rather than to voters right away.
The appointments and the Lanni Orchards lease are routine board business that residents affected by those committees or that farm property may want to track.
